why: The criterion holds for all ten expect lines. Each one can be checked at the PR head before merge, and none needs a release, deploy, publish or anything else that only exists after merge. Eight lines have "run" proofs that run `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` on temporary files, read `package.json` with `node -e`, or run `npm ci && npm test`. Each states a clear expected result, such as "expect exit=1 and exactly the lines 2, 4, 5", so one reader gets one answer. The CI line says to "Read the `test` check on the PR head commit", which exists before merge. The README line is a "read" of the "What is here" section at the head. The test-coverage line adds reading the test files for the four named cases, which is still one reader's job at the head. Publishing to npm is listed as a non-goal, so no line depends on it.
